summary: Configured node1 (Ubuntu 16.04) to require new user passwords be at least 12 characters with at least 3 character classes, via libpam-pwquality (minlen=12, minclass=3) wired into /etc/pam.d/common-password ahead of pam_unix. Verified enforcement live (reject short password, reject low-diversity password, accept compliant password) both before and after a full node reboot, and confirmed the boot identity actually changed across the restart. Test users were created and cleaned up afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 16.04) and existing PAM config (cmd-96796d3edbb84e29)
Installed libpam-pwquality via apt (cmd-464d75eff0d64ed2, cmd-a8468357854e4759), which auto-wired pam_pwquality.so requisite into common-password before pam_unix (cmd-351f80ca8ca24e4f)
Confirmed PAM stack ordering: pwquality requisite before pam_unix use_authtok (cmd-909775d8123244f4)

Created test user pwtestuser and validated: root-set weak password bypasses check (expected root override, cmd-20038d2db7f3407e); set known initial password (cmd-1e46aecd6dd74be8); self-service change with <12 chars rejected (cmd-fd1d94daad9d429f); self-service change with 12+ chars but <3 classes rejected (cmd-aa2eba635bce4151); self-service change meeting both rules accepted (cmd-a11b60314b1343f9)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and config state (cmd-c6b2c629647540e6, cmd-da4dd10e361945ac)
Issued reboot via nohup shutdown -r now with ack returned before disconnect (cmd-2641e970a1e7472e)
Confirmed node went unreachable during reboot (cmd-1b2f6f4cdc30470c) then polled until available again with new boot_id (cmd-a76d00fda4de40b3), proving an actual restart
Verified PAM/pwquality config persisted after reboot (cmd-5816a2de9b7a44f6)
Re-validated live enforcement post-reboot with a new test user pwtestuser2: initial password set (cmd-cd6e830a38764ea7), weak self-service change rejected on length (cmd-3d25a26e26a94291)
